newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends down on institutional selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends down on institutional selling.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended sharply down on Monday, with the key September 1996 contract closing limit-down on institutional selling, traders said.
The September ended at an intra-day low of 2,514 yuan ($302) per tonne, losing 90 yuan. It opened at a high of 2,600.
Combined volume rose to 27,300 tonnes from 18,550.
Traders said some institutions built short positions at high levels due to lower spot rice prices in Shanghai, currently around 2,400 yuan per tonne.
"Futures prices are much higher than spot prices, especially considering that now is the grain-harvesting season," one trader said.
Traders said there were also rumours that the inventory on the Shanghai Cereals and Oils Exchange was rising, which helped to depress investor confidence.
Figures for the inventory were not available.
Traders said that there was more room for rice futures to fall than to rise in the next few days.
